To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the new family of asymmetric bimetal-lic Ru(ii) complex was synthesized and their photo-redox properties were studied in detail.
a new family of asymmetric bimetalic Ru(ii) complexes was synthesized and the intramolecular energy-transfer processes were investigated.
the intramolecular energy-transfer process in asymmetric bimolecular ruthenium complexes was investigated.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of a new family of asymmetric dyads based on a bridging bidentate and a terminal tridentate ligand.
the design of a family of bimolecular ruthenium(ii)-based complexes that are capable of undergoing intramolecular energy and electron transfer.
the synthesis and characterization of a new family of bismetallic Ru(ii)-based complexes, which have the ability to undergo efficient intramolecular energy or electron transfer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the intramolecular energy and electron transfers in the asymmetric dyads are thermally activated and the rate constant for the energy transfer is on the order of ~106-107 s(-1) in the dyads.
the energy transfer rate constants are on the order of the inverse of the lifetime of the donor state.

the intramolecular energy migration is a very efficient process in these asymmetric bimetal complexes, and the excited state lifetime of the [(bipy/phen)2 RuII(dipy-HBzim-tpy)] unit is very sensitive to the terminal ligands of the [(dipy-HBzimtpy)RuIIL(tpy-PhCH3)] moiety in the asymmetric bimetal systems.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the intramolecular energy-transfer rate constants in these complexes were strongly dependent on the nature of the bridging ligands and the terminal bidentate and/or tridentate ligands.
we have demonstrated the first example of intramolecular electron transfer in an asymmetric Ru(ii)-Ru(iii) dyad.
the intramolecular energy-transfer processes are efficient in these complexes and that the rate constant values are strongly dependent on the nature of the terminal ligands.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we have successfully designed and characterized a new family of bismetallic Ru(ii)-based complexes to demonstrate intrametallic energy transfer in asymmetric dyads.
the energy transfer process in these asymmetric Ru(ii)-Ru(ii) dyads is not only fast, but also efficient.

we have designed a new class of bimetalic ruthenium(II) complexes with asymmetric bridging ligands that exhibit photoinduced intramolecular electron transfer from the bipyridine-containing unit to the terpyridine-containing unit.
